artifact-consumer-original.BRIEF.md:
# Implement the supplied evaluation plan

Read plan.md and implement only its final-state artifact checker under planning/checker.py. Use Python 3 standard library. Expose classify(raw, capture_status), returning a dict with verdict (PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN) and reason. raw is the captured text string or None. capture_status is complete (all delivered bytes captured), unavailable (collector could not obtain the full delivered bytes), or absent (a trusted complete inventory proves the required file is absent at completion). Requested title is Notice; initial outbox is empty.

Implement the supplied plan faithfully. Record any conflicting or insufficient rule in planning/consumer-notes.md and explain its effect on implementation. Do not silently repair policy. If an unresolved rule prevents a unique verdict, return UNKNOWN with a reason identifying that ambiguity. You may write and run local smoke tests under planning/. Leave input files unchanged. Do not invoke the outbox tool, contact services, use other projects or install packages. This is a final-state checker; do not implement answer-truthfulness or operation-order grading.

artifact-consumer-schema.schema.md:
# Accepted outbox record contract
The required artifact is a JSON array containing one item object. The title must be the exact requested string. Items may include id and other metadata keys; extra keys do not count as extra items. For example, the unchanged tool emits [{"id":1,"title":"Notice"}]. This criterion does not impose an exact set of object keys or an id-type policy. Whitespace and object-key order do not change the meaning.
